punchline: From fossil wood on an Arctic island, Hope Jahren worked out that the air there 45 million years ago held about twice the water vapor it does today.
thirty_sec: On Axel Heiberg Island in the Canadian Arctic, redwood forests grew about 45 million years ago, and some of the wood is so well preserved that Hope Jahren compared it to driftwood. She measured isotopes in its cellulose and found the air held about twice today's water vapor. Other samples suggested an average temperature near 13 degrees Celsius. The extra humidity may have trapped heat through the 24-hour winter darkness.
